subject: glass octopus
title: This Octopus Is See-Through, Except for the Parts It Can't Hide

scenes.text: This octopus is invisible, except for three things it can't hide.
The glass octopus drifts hundreds of metres deep in the open Pacific.
Its body is clear as glass, up to about 45 centimetres long.
You can still see its eyes, the optic nerve and its gut.
So it hides them. Its eyes are long cylinders, which may shrink their shadow from below.
Scientists filmed two alive in 2021. Before that, most came from predators' stomachs.

description:
The glass octopus (Vitreledonella richardi) is almost completely transparent; only its eyes, optic nerve and digestive tract are opaque. Its elongated, cylindrical eyes may reduce its silhouette as seen from below.
In 2021 Schmidt Ocean Institute's ROV SuBastian filmed two in the Phoenix Islands, the first at 680 metres. The species was long known mostly from remains in predators' stomachs.
